findings.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") twice, so rawTokenId is never null-checked and a null rawTokenId passes validation with the wrong message text. A caller constructing AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId (e.g. a future encoder provider passing an unset ID) silently produces a context whose encoded token id ends in ':null' or 'null'-suffixed ids instead of failing fast at the guard the class was written to provide.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId checks items[0].substring(3, 5) for the grant shortcut (the grant occupies chars 4-5 of the 6-char context) and the condition is inverted (returns false when it matches), so the grant assertion never rejects a token and would reject every correct token if the offset were fixed. The four upgraded event expectations (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) verify nothing about the encoded grant: any regression that encodes the wrong grant, or encodes 'na' because a grant path forgot to set Constants.GRANT_TYPE, passes CI silently.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId has no production caller in this diff — the framework encodes context into every access token ID (changing the jti/TOKEN_ID format from a bare UUID to 'onrtac:<uuid>' globally, as evidenced by the AssertEvents updates) yet nothing in-tree ever decodes it. Every access token ID and event TOKEN_ID detail changes format for all external consumers (event storage, admin tooling, anything asserting UUID jti) while the retrieval side is ships-inert; if the consuming feature never lands, the format change bought nothing and is hard to walk back because already-issued tokens carry the new format.

[ADVISORY] Grant-type propagation into Constants.GRANT_TYPE is incomplete across token-issuing paths: the diff sets it in OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ROPC, PreAuthorizedCode, refresh validateToken, and StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient only, leaving other createClientAccessToken callers (e.g. the legacy/abstract token exchange paths in AbstractTokenExchangeProvider, including exchangeClientToClient) unset. Tokens issued on the uncovered paths encode grant shortcut 'na' instead of their real grant; because the AssertEvents matcher is vacuous (separate finding), no integration test can detect this, and the encoded context silently misreports grant provenance for exactly the paths that were not hand-audited.

[ADVISORY] The postInit duplicate-shortcut validation only compares map sizes, which does not catch a grant shortcut colliding with another grant's ID or with the reserved 'na' value (both added after the check), so a collision can pass validation yet produce an ambiguous encode/decode round-trip. When a future grant implementation is added whose shortcut equals an existing grant's ID (or 'na'), postInit passes, but encodeTokenId for one grant and getTokenContextFromTokenId for the same string resolve to different grant types — a silent misdecode that the check exists precisely to prevent.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId reads the grant shortcut from substring(3,5) (the last char of tokenType plus the first char of the grant shortcut, e.g. "tc" for "trltcc") instead of substring(4,6), and the comparison is inverted (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), so the grant assertion is vacuous. Every updated expectation (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) passes for ANY 6-char prefix followed by a UUID, so the new integration assertions added to verify that token IDs encode the correct grant never verify anything; conversely, a token whose chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected shortcut would be wrongly rejected. The feature's only end-to-end verification is a no-op.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice; the second call, intended to validate rawTokenId (message says "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), re-validates grantType, so rawTokenId is never null-checked. An AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId passes construction and encodeTokenId emits a token ID ending in ':null', producing a syntactically valid but unusable token identifier instead of failing fast at the point of error.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut register shortcuts into grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without re-running the duplicate-shortcut validation enforced in postInit, and a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the previous grant's entry in grantsByShortcuts while grantsToShortcuts retains both. When a newly deployed grant's shortcut collides with an existing one, whichever grant triggers the lazy path first wins nondeterministically, and decode of already-issued tokens (getTokenContextFromTokenId) starts returning the wrong grant type for the displaced shortcut — exactly the failure the postInit IllegalStateException exists to prevent, bypassed at runtime.

[ADVISORY] The test bypasses postInit and hand-builds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts with only two grants, so the factory's shortcut-registration loop and duplicate-shortcut validation branch have zero test coverage, and testIncorrectGrantType's 'ofrtac:5678' case conflates 'shortcut absent from the hand-built map' with 'invalid grant' — 'ac' is the authorization_code shortcut that a real factory registers. A regression in postInit (e.g. a broken duplicate-shortcut check or a mapping-loop bug) ships undetected, and the test suite gives false confidence that invalid-grant rejection is verified when it only verifies lookup misses against an artificially truncated registry.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId is declared and implemented but has no production caller anywhere in this diff — no code ever parses the context back out of a token ID; only the test invokes it. The decode half of the framework ships inert: no behavior depends on the encoding being correct, so any defect in the format (segment layout, shortcut collisions, legacy-ID handling) surfaces only when a future consumer lands, by which point the 6-char wire format is already baked into issued tokens and cannot be changed without breaking them.

[ADVISORY] The public Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted outright instead of being updated to also copy the new grantType field. Any out-of-tree provider (server-spi-private consumers, custom grant implementations) that constructs a Context from an existing one fails at compile time on upgrade, and even in-tree callers that legitimately need to clone a request context now have no way to carry grantType along — the field is silently lost in any manual field-by-field copy.

[ADVISORY] Setting the GRANT_TYPE attribute is scattered across individual call sites (createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, validateToken, StandardTokenExchangeProvider) with no enforcement at the single funnel point (initToken), so any token-issuing path the author failed to patch is indistinguishable, by design, from a genuinely unknown grant — both encode 'na'. The framework's core invariant — 'the token ID reflects the grant that produced the token' — is not enforced anywhere; each new issuing path (e.g. a future token-exchange subclass or a new grant that bypasses OAuth2GrantTypeBase) silently degrades to 'na' unless a developer remembers to hand-patch it, and nothing (compile check, test, or default) catches the omission.

[BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher reads the grant shortcut from substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6) and then inverts the comparison ('if (...equals(expected)) return false'), so it accepts every well-formed encoded token ID regardless of which grant shortcut is embedded and would reject a correctly-matching one. Stand-in-guard failure: the four assertions that are supposed to verify the new grant-context encoding (expectCodeToToken 'ac', expectDeviceCodeToToken 'dg', expectRefresh 'rt', expectAuthReqIdToToken 'ci') degenerate to a plain 'prefix:UUID' check — the suite stays green even if initToken encodes the wrong grant (or none) into every access token ID; the guard the diff exists to provide can go green while production encoding is wrong. (Mechanically the two errors cancel on the happy path: for TT in {rt,lt,un} the sliced chars TT[1]+GT[0] can never equal a valid 2-char grant shortcut, so the inverted branch is never taken.)

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the second check intended for rawTokenId validates grantType again, so a null rawTokenId passes validation and produces a token ID of the form 'xxxyy?:null'. The stated invariant ('Null rawTokenId not allowed') is not enforced; a null rawTokenId flows into encodeTokenId and yields a syntactically valid but meaningless token ID 'onrtac:null' that round-trips through getTokenContextFromTokenId as rawTokenId="null", colliding across all tokens minted with a null id. Latent today (the only call site passes KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()) but the guard is the contract and it checks the wrong variable.

[ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares map sizes before registering the reserved 'na' sentinel, and a grant whose shortcut is 'na' produces equal sizes at check time, so it passes validation and is then silently overwritten by grantsByShortcuts.put("na", "na"). A third-party grant type with shortcut 'na' is accepted at startup with no error, but its tokens are encoded with the UNKNOWN shortcut and every such token decodes as grantType=UNKNOWN — silent misattribution of grant context in the token ID with no diagnostic; the invariant 'Shortcut should be unique across grants' is not actually enforced against the reserved value.

[ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut mutate the shared registry from request threads without re-running the duplicate-shortcut validation, and are unreachable in production because all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances are registered before postInit iterates them. Speculative generality that bypasses the startup invariant: if the path ever does execute (e.g. a provider registered after postInit), a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing grantsByShortcuts entry — two grant names then resolve through the same shortcut and decode ambiguously — with no IllegalStateException like the postInit path throws. Deleting the two lazy branches removes two unvalidated mutation sites and the divergent behavior; the test suite already exercises the maps without them.

[ADVISORY] The invariant 'every minted access token carries Constants.GRANT_TYPE' is enforced only by convention across five scattered write sites (createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, and the hardcoded OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN in TokenManager.validateToken), with silent 'na' fallback rather than an error when a site is missed. The next grant-like flow (or a new minting path that bypasses createTokenResponse, as ROPC and PreAuthorizedCode already do) silently encodes grant shortcut 'na' into every token ID it mints — no failure, no log, just permanently wrong context for those tokens; the ownership of the attribution rule lives in N call sites instead of one (e.g. in the encoder itself or a single attach point), and the encodeTokenId path cannot distinguish 'legitimately unknown' from 'forgotten'.

[ADVISORY] The access token jti silently changes from a bare 36-char UUID to a 43-char 'xxxyyz:<uuid>' composite for every minted token, changing a value external parties see and persist. Resource servers, audit pipelines, and integrations that store or column-size jti as a UUID (CHAR(36), UUID column type, UUID regex validation) will truncate, reject, or misparse every access token ID issued after upgrade; the diff updates Keycloak's own internal matcher but the wire-visible format of a public token field changes with no versioning or opt-out.

[ADVISORY] Decode failure handling is asymmetric: a legacy no-colon ID degrades gracefully to UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN, but a well-formed 6-char context with an unregistered shortcut throws IllegalArgumentException instead of degrading the same way. Tokens legitimately minted while a grant provider was deployed become hard errors if that provider is later removed (extension uninstalled, rolling deploy where the validating node lacks the grant) — the lazy map-refresh only helps while the provider exists; the same class of token gets two diametrically opposite treatments (silent degrade vs throw) depending on whether the string contains a colon.

[ADVISORY] The sessionType/tokenType derivation logic (TRANSIENT vs offline-vs-online branching, and the newly-public static getShouldUseLightweightToken call) has no test anywhere in this diff — the unit test only covers encode/decode of grant shortcuts. A regression in the derivation (e.g. offline sessions classified ONLINE, or the lightweight check reading the wrong session attribute) would stamp the wrong 4-char prefix into every minted token ID across all grants; nothing in the diff's tests would catch it, and the encoded prefix is what downstream consumers of getTokenContextFromTokenId will trust.

[BUG] isAccessTokenId checks items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) and inverts the comparison (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), so the grant-shortcut assertion it was introduced to provide is vacuous. The review iteration that replaced isUUID() with isAccessTokenId in expectCodeToToken/expectRefresh/expectDeviceCodeToToken/expectAuthReqIdToToken silently weakened, not strengthened, the assertion: with the wrong offset the equals() almost never fires, so every token ID passes as long as the raw suffix is a UUID — a regression that encodes the wrong grant shortcut (or drops encoding entirely, since a colon-less ID still passes the split/isUUID path only if it splits into 2 parts... actually a UUID has no colon so items.length==1 and it returns false; but any 6-char prefix with a wrong grant passes). The PR's own regression net for the core feature does not verify the feature's output.

[BUG] The constructor validates grantType twice (`Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed")` followed by `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")`), so rawTokenId is never null-checked. A null rawTokenId passes construction and produces a token ID ending in the literal string ':null' via string concatenation in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, and later decoding yields rawTokenId "null" instead of failing fast — the validation intent stated by the message string is silently not implemented.

[ADVISORY] The public copy constructor Context(Context) was deleted and grantType is now snapshotted from formParams only in the primary constructor, while the retained setFormParams() mutator does not refresh it. Out-of-tree custom grant providers that copy Context instances (a previously supported pattern on this SPI class) break at compile time on upgrade with no migration note; any in-tree or external caller that replaces form params via setFormParams after construction gets a stale grantType, so the encoded token ID carries the wrong grant shortcut with no error.

[ADVISORY] Setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE is hand-maintained at five separate call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, TokenManager.validateToken) instead of being centralized where clientSessionCtx is assembled — and the ROPC explicit set is redundant because its flow already routes through createTokenResponse. Every future token-issuing path must remember to set the attribute at the right point; one that forgets it silently encodes the 'na' UNKNOWN shortcut into real token IDs with no warning, defeating the framework's stated purpose of reliably retrieving context from the token.

[ADVISORY] The access token jti format changes globally from a UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' unconditionally — no feature flag, realm option, or provider default gates the new encoding. All realms and all clients are affected the moment this version deploys; external consumers that correlate, log, or persist access-token jti values as UUIDs (event listeners, resource servers, audit tooling) silently receive a different format, and operators cannot revert the behavior without a code rollback.

[ADVISORY] The entire decode direction of the framework (getTokenContextFromTokenId, plus the lazy shortcut-registration refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut) has no production caller in this diff — only the unit tests exercise it. Roughly half the new provider surface ships inert: decode behavior, error messages, and the runtime map-mutation refresh paths evolve with no integration coverage and no consumer to keep them honest, and the first future consumer inherits untested code paths (including IllegalStateException on re-encoding old tokens decoded as UNKNOWN).

[ADVISORY] grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts are declared package-private with no modifiers solely so DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest can assign them directly, bypassing postInit's real initialization and validation. The registry's invariants (uniqueness validation, the 'na' entries, ConcurrentHashMap choice) are not exercised by the test that pretends to cover the encoder; a future change to field types or names breaks test compilation, and the test's hand-built map diverges from what postInit actually produces, masking real wiring defects.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId decodes security-relevant context (sessionType, tokenType, grantType) from an arbitrary string with no integrity check, and throws IllegalArgumentException on any malformed/unknown shortcut in client-supplied input. The 6-char context prefix carries no MAC and is trivially forgeable by anyone who can supply a token id string: the first endpoint that calls this decoder on user input (revocation, introspection, admin lookup) gets attacker-controlled sessionType/grantType labels (e.g. a caller-supplied 'of...' id claims an offline-session token) and simultaneously converts malformed ids into uncaught IllegalArgumentException -> HTTP 500 instead of a 4xx, with the attacker-controlled id echoed in the exception message. Any future consumer that makes authorization or session-lifetime decisions from the decoded context inherits a spoofable input by design.

[ADVISORY] The runtime lazy-registration paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut insert grant<->shortcut mappings into the shared maps without the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit performs, so a later-deployed grant provider silently overwrites an existing shortcut mapping. When a custom/third-party OAuth2GrantType whose shortcut collides with an existing one (or whose id collides with an existing shortcut) is deployed after startup, grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) overwrites the previous entry in the process-wide ConcurrentHashMap; every previously issued token id carrying that shortcut then decodes to the wrong grant type, and getGrantTypeByShortcut additionally picks among colliding factories with a nondeterministic stream findFirst(). The startup IllegalStateException check at lines 80-83 never runs again after postInit, so the corruption is silent and persists until restart.

[ADVISORY] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never validates rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes construction and encodeTokenId silently emits a token id ending in the literal string ':null'. The second check on line 71 was clearly meant to guard rawTokenId; as written, a caller that constructs an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets no error at construction and produces a jti whose unique-id suffix is the constant string 'null' -- colliding across every such token and defeating any per-token use of the id (revocation, event correlation). Latent today because the only in-diff caller passes KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), but the guard the code visibly intends to provide does not exist.

[BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher checks the wrong character positions AND inverts the comparison: `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` reads chars 4-5 (second char of tokenType + first char of grantType) instead of chars 5-6 (substring(4,6) where the grant shortcut lives), and it returns false when the shortcut MATCHES instead of when it mismatches. The grant-type assertion is inert in both directions: no real encoded prefix (st2+tt2+gt2, e.g. 'onrtac') can have chars at index 3-4 equal to any registered shortcut ('ac','cc','rt','ci','dg','ro','pg','te','pc'), so `matchesSafely` falls through to the UUID check and accepts ANY '<6chars>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of which grant type (or no grant type at all) was encoded. Every updated expectation (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) therefore passes even if TokenManager/initToken encodes the wrong grant, no grant, or a scrambled prefix — the suite gives false confidence that the new context encoding works end-to-end. Note also that fixing only the index while keeping the inverted compare would make every valid token FAIL, so the matcher as committed demonstrably never validated real encoder output.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the fourth check at line 72 duplicates the grantType check (line 71) instead of checking rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted. A caller passing null rawTokenId bypasses validation and later produces a token id like 'onrtna:null' from encodeTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java line ~120 concatenates getRawTokenId() unconditionally); no test in the diff covers this because the unit tests only pass literal non-null ids. The bug is self-evidencing: the error message even says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' while the code checks grantType.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the encode direction that TokenManager.initToken (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java, initToken change at lines ~1048-1054) actually uses in production — is exercised by no test in this diff; only the decode direction is unit-tested. The branching logic that classifies tokens (TRANSIENT vs isOffline vs ONLINE, getShouldUseLightweightToken, null GRANT_TYPE attribute -> UNKNOWN) is the code that runs on every issued access token, and a regression there (e.g. misclassifying offline sessions, or reading the attribute under the wrong key) produces systematically wrong encoded token ids with no failing test. Evidence of absence: checked services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java (only calls getTokenContextFromTokenId and encodeTokenId on hand-built AccessTokenContext values) and testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java (whose matcher, per the bug above, verifies only 'prefix:uuid' shape).

[ADVISORY] The test setup hand-populates the package-private maps `factory.grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` and never calls postInit, so the factory's real registration logic — the duplicate-shortcut validation in postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java postInit, IllegalStateException check) and the lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut — has zero coverage. A future grant factory added with a shortcut colliding with an existing one (exactly the failure mode the postInit validation comment says it exists for) ships undetected, and the cluster-rolling-deploy lazy-refresh code paths (getShortcutByGrantType falling through to sessionFactory.getProviderFactory) — which contain non-trivial concurrency-prone map mutation — run in production with no test ever having executed them. The need to bypass postInit in the test is itself a smell: the maps are initialized in postInit rather than init, making the factory untestable without field-poking.

[ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType catches broad RuntimeException with an empty 'ignored' handler and asserts nothing about the exception type or message, so any RuntimeException — including an NPE thrown by a bug in the parsing code rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException — passes the test. A regression that turns the deliberate IllegalArgumentException for a bad grant shortcut into an accidental NPE or IndexOutOfBoundsException (e.g. from substring on a malformed prefix) keeps this test green, and the '// ignored' handler swallows the evidence; the variable is even named 'iae' while catching RuntimeException, showing the intended narrower contract was loosened during writing.

[BUG] The constructor validates grantType twice — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` is repeated on the line that was meant to check rawTokenId — so a null rawTokenId passes validation unchallenged. A caller constructing an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets no validation failure; encodeTokenId then concatenates the null, minting a token id like 'onrtac:null' (string 'null' as the jti) instead of failing fast. No current caller in this diff passes null, so it is latent, but the guard this new public API promises does not exist for rawTokenId.

[ADVISORY] Token-ID decoding is asymmetric across deployment transitions: legacy colonless IDs degrade gracefully to UNKNOWN context, but an encoded ID whose grant shortcut no longer maps (grant provider uninstalled/renamed between deployments) throws IllegalArgumentException from getTokenContextFromTokenId. Tokens issued while a (custom or later-removed) grant provider was registered persist their 2-char shortcut inside the id; after that provider is removed, any caller of getTokenContextFromTokenId — the method's stated purpose is to read context back out of long-lived tokens — gets an IllegalArgumentException instead of a UNKNOWN-context fallback, the exact treatment the same method grants to pre-upgrade UUID ids. The one migration-compat path built into this design (legacy IDs) is not applied to the second class of pre-existing data it will encounter: IDs minted by providers that no longer exist.

[ADVISORY] initToken silently changes the persisted/emitted token identifier format from a 36-char UUID to a 43+ char 'prefix:uuid' form with no consumer-side compatibility step beyond the in-server decoder fallback. Every consumer that stores or joins on access-token ids — event-store TOKEN_ID details (the diff itself has to rewrite AssertEvents matchers for exactly this reason), external audit pipelines, or any tooling keyed on UUID format — receives a structurally different identifier after upgrade with no versioning or opt-out; records written before the upgrade (bare UUIDs) and after (prefixed) become a mixed-format column for such consumers.

[BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice; the second call passes grantType with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId passes the guard instead of failing fast, and encodeTokenId string-concats it into a literal token ID ending in ':null' (e.g. 'onrtac:null'); the only defense is the double-check that was supposed to reject it, so a caller passing a null raw ID gets a silently corrupt token identity rather than the NPE the guard promises.

[ADVISORY] GRANT_TYPE is only populated at the four explicit setAttribute sites (createTokenResponse, TokenManager.validateToken, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType); any token-issuance path that builds its response outside these sites silently encodes grant context as UNKNOWN. Tokens issued on a path that does not route through createTokenResponse (e.g. token-exchange flows handled in AbstractTokenExchangeProvider outside exchangeClientToOIDCClient, or grant types that build AccessTokenResponseBuilder directly) get 'na' encoded in their jti with no log and no error — the encoder's purpose (distinguishing grant context from the token ID) silently degrades exactly on the paths someone forgot to touch, and nobody can detect it because UNKNOWN is a first-class accepted value that encodes and decodes successfully.

[ADVISORY] The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut puts into the maps with no duplicate-shortcut check, so a runtime-discovered grant factory whose shortcut collides with an existing grant's shortcut silently overwrites the existing mapping that postInit's size-comparison validation was written to prevent. If a colliding grant factory ever reaches this lazy path, tokens of the displaced grant still encode with the old shortcut but decode (getGrantTypeByShortcut) to the new grant's ID — grant type is silently misattributed on decode with no error, the exact corruption the postInit IllegalStateException exists to catch; the check-then-put race between two concurrent first-encounters is benign, but the overwrite is not. Also note this lazy path is effectively unreachable under the normal Keycloak lifecycle (postInit already enumerates all OAuth2GrantTypeFactories via getProviderFactoriesStream), making it dead defensive code carrying this footgun.

[ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId has an inconsistent failure shape: an ID with no colon degrades gracefully to UNKNOWN context (the legacy-token path), but any ID containing a colon whose prefix is not exactly 6 chars — or with unknown 2-char shortcuts — throws an unchecked IllegalArgumentException, and no caller in this diff catches it. The method's entire purpose is decoding token IDs it did not mint (legacy tokens, and eventually client-presented jtis in validation/introspection flows); whoever wires the first production caller and feeds it a token whose jti is not exactly '6chars:uuid' — a foreign-issuer token like 'abc:def', or a truncated value — gets a raw RuntimeException propagated up the request path as a 500 where a 4xx/handled-rejection belongs, while legacy UUIDs silently work, so the failure only appears for a subset of malformed inputs and is easy to ship untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new isAccessTokenId matcher reads the grant shortcut from substring(3,5) instead of substring(4,6) and then inverts the comparison ('if (...equals(expected)) return false'), so it accepts every well-formed encoded token ID regardless of which grant shortcut is embedded and would reject a correctly-matching one. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The duplicate-shortcut validation compares map sizes before registering the reserved 'na' sentinel, and a grant whose shortcut is 'na' produces equal sizes at check time, so it passes validation and is then silently overwritten by grantsByShortcuts.put("na", "na"). A third-party grant type with shortcut 'na' is accepted at startup with no error, but its tokens are encoded with the UNKNOWN shortcut and every such token decodes as grantType=UNKNOWN — silent misattribution of grant context in the token ID with no diagnostic; the invariant 'Shortcut should be unique across grants' is not actually enforced against the reserved value.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(), the reserved UNKNOWN/sentinel mapping is added *before* the duplicate-shortcut validation: `grantsByShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN); grantsToShortcuts.put(UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN);` and only then `if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) throw ...`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy 'refresh maps' branches in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut mutate the shared registry from request threads without re-running the duplicate-shortcut validation, and are unreachable in production because all OAuth2GrantTypeFactory instances are registered before postInit iterates them. Speculative generality that bypasses the startup invariant: if the path ever does execute (e.g. a provider registered after postInit), a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing grantsByShortcuts entry — two grant names then resolve through the same shortcut and decode ambiguously — with no IllegalStateException like the postInit path throws. Deleting the two lazy branches removes two unvalidated mutation sites and the divergent behavior; the test suite already exercises the maps without them.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, the lazy “refresh maps” paths in getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() (both in this diff) mutate the shared ConcurrentHashMap registries (grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts) via put() without any re-validation of shortcut uniqueness like the postInit() size-check does. If a newly discovered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returns a shortcut already present, the put() silently overwrites the existing mapping, making shortcut→grant decoding ambiguous and violating the invariant enforced at startup. Whether the branch is common/reachable can’t be proven from the diff, but the unvalidated overwrite behavior in that code path is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The invariant 'every minted access token carries Constants.GRANT_TYPE' is enforced only by convention across five scattered write sites (createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, and the hardcoded OAuth2Constants.REFRESH_TOKEN in TokenManager.validateToken), with silent 'na' fallback rather than an error when a site is missed. The next grant-like flow (or a new minting path that bypasses createTokenResponse, as ROPC and PreAuthorizedCode already do) silently encodes grant shortcut 'na' into every token ID it mints — no failure, no log, just permanently wrong context for those tokens; the ownership of the attribution rule lives in N call sites instead of one (e.g. in the encoder itself or a single attach point), and the encodeTokenId path cannot distinguish 'legitimately unknown' from 'forgotten'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new implicit invariant: TokenManager.initToken() now always encodes the access token ID via TokenContextEncoderProvider using context derived from ClientSessionContext (TokenManager#initToken). The encoder reads Constants.GRANT_TYPE from the client session context and, if missing, silently falls back to "na" (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext). The attribute is set in several scattered places (OAuth2GrantTypeBase#createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType#process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType#process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider#exchangeClientToOIDCClient, TokenManager#validateToken for refresh). This makes correctness depend on all minting paths remembering to set the attribute, and missing it will quietly encode "na" rather than fail or log, making it hard to detect forgotten wiring. However, from the diff alone we cannot prove an actual current minting path is missing the setAttribute call, so this is an architectural/robustness concern rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The access token jti silently changes from a bare 36-char UUID to a 43-char 'xxxyyz:<uuid>' composite for every minted token, changing a value external parties see and persist. Resource servers, audit pipelines, and integrations that store or column-size jti as a UUID (CHAR(36), UUID column type, UUID regex validation) will truncate, reject, or misparse every access token ID issued after upgrade; the diff updates Keycloak's own internal matcher but the wire-visible format of a public token field changes with no versioning or opt-out.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change newly minted access token IDs from a bare UUID to a composite `prefix:rawId` format. In `TokenManager.initToken`, `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` is replaced by `token.id(encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx))`, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` returns `sessionType+tokenType+grantShortcut+ ':' + rawTokenId` (e.g., `trltcc:1234`). This is a wire-visible change to the token `id`/`jti` value with no config/opt-out shown in the diff, and tests are updated to expect the new format (`AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)`). However, the diff does not show this as an unintended defect—it's an intentional behavioral/API change—so it is best classified as a non-bug but important compatibility concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Decode failure handling is asymmetric: a legacy no-colon ID degrades gracefully to UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN, but a well-formed 6-char context with an unregistered shortcut throws IllegalArgumentException instead of degrading the same way. Tokens legitimately minted while a grant provider was deployed become hard errors if that provider is later removed (extension uninstalled, rolling deploy where the validating node lacks the grant) — the lazy map-refresh only helps while the provider exists; the same class of token gets two diametrically opposite treatments (silent degrade vs throw) depending on whether the string contains a colon.

adjudication.rationale: The asymmetry is verifiable in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(...)`: if there is no `:` it returns an `AccessTokenContext` with `UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN/na`, but if there is a colon it enforces strict decoding and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for unknown session/token/grant shortcuts (e.g., `gt == null` leads to throw). Since grant shortcuts are populated from deployed `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementations in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit(...)`, removing a grant provider would indeed make previously-issued token IDs with that shortcut fail to decode rather than degrade to UNKNOWN. However, the diff does not show this decode path being used in critical validation flows, so the impact is an edge-case/backwards-compat/design concern rather than a definitively proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The sessionType/tokenType derivation logic (TRANSIENT vs offline-vs-online branching, and the newly-public static getShouldUseLightweightToken call) has no test anywhere in this diff — the unit test only covers encode/decode of grant shortcuts. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] isAccessTokenId checks items[0].substring(3, 5) instead of substring(4, 6) and inverts the comparison (`if (...equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`), so the grant-shortcut assertion it was introduced to provide is vacuous. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Setting Constants.GRANT_TYPE is hand-maintained at five separate call sites (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, TokenManager.validateToken) instead of being centralized where clientSessionCtx is assembled — and the ROPC explicit set is redundant because its flow already routes through createTokenResponse. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The access token jti format changes globally from a UUID to '<6-char-context>:<uuid>' unconditionally — no feature flag, realm option, or provider default gates the new encoding. All realms and all clients are affected the moment this version deploys; external consumers that correlate, log, or persist access-token jti values as UUIDs (event listeners, resource servers, audit tooling) silently receive a different format, and operators cannot revert the behavior without a code rollback.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes access token `jti` generation globally in `TokenManager.initToken()` from `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()` (UUID) to `encoder.encodeTokenId(tokenCtx)` where `encodeTokenId` produces a `<6 chars>:<rawId>` format (see `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId`). A default provider is registered via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.encode.TokenContextEncoderProviderFactory` and the SPI is added to `org.keycloak.provider.Spi`, with no feature flag/realm/client option shown to preserve the old UUID-only format. Tests are updated to expect the new format (`AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId(...)`), reinforcing that this is intended global behavior. This is a concrete backward-compatibility/operational concern, but not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire decode direction of the framework (getTokenContextFromTokenId, plus the lazy shortcut-registration refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut) has no production caller in this diff — only the unit tests exercise it. adjudication.rationale: In this diff, the new provider is used in production only for encoding token IDs: TokenManager.initToken() calls encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...) and encoder.encodeTokenId(...). adjudication.rationale: In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`, `grantsByShortcuts` and `grantsToShortcuts` are declared with no access modifier (package-private), and the new test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` directly assigns them (`factory.grantsByShortcuts = new HashMap<>()`, then builds `grantsToShortcuts`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId decodes security-relevant context (sessionType, tokenType, grantType) from an arbitrary string with no integrity check, and throws IllegalArgumentException on any malformed/unknown shortcut in client-supplied input. The 6-char context prefix carries no MAC and is trivially forgeable by anyone who can supply a token id string: the first endpoint that calls this decoder on user input (revocation, introspection, admin lookup) gets attacker-controlled sessionType/grantType labels (e.g. a caller-supplied 'of...' id claims an offline-session token) and simultaneously converts malformed ids into uncaught IllegalArgumentException -> HTTP 500 instead of a 4xx, with the attacker-controlled id echoed in the exception message. Any future consumer that makes authorization or session-lifetime decisions from the decoded context inherits a spoofable input by design.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId(String)` which parses a caller-provided string and may throw `IllegalArgumentException` with the input echoed, but the finding’s security claims are not grounded in the shown changes: (1) the encoded token id is generated server-side in `TokenManager#initToken` via `encodeTokenId(...)` and then carried inside a signed token, so the context prefix is not “trivially forgeable by anyone who can supply a token id string” in the normal flow; (2) the diff does not show any endpoint/consumer (introspection/revocation/admin lookup) calling `getTokenContextFromTokenId` on client-supplied input, nor any uncaught exception path leading to HTTP 500. The described exploit/impact therefore relies on usage not present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The runtime lazy-registration paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut insert grant<->shortcut mappings into the shared maps without the duplicate-shortcut validation that postInit performs, so a later-deployed grant provider silently overwrites an existing shortcut mapping. When a custom/third-party OAuth2GrantType whose shortcut collides with an existing one (or whose id collides with an existing shortcut) is deployed after startup, grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) overwrites the previous entry in the process-wide ConcurrentHashMap; every previously issued token id carrying that shortcut then decodes to the wrong grant type, and getGrantTypeByShortcut additionally picks among colliding factories with a nondeterministic stream findFirst(). The startup IllegalStateException check at lines 80-83 never runs again after postInit, so the corruption is silent and persists until restart.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() validates duplicates only once via the size comparison after initially populating grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts. However, both lazy refresh paths can later mutate these shared ConcurrentHashMaps without any duplicate-shortcut (or id/shortcut) validation: getShortcutByGrantType() does unconditional grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) and grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut) when a new grantType appears, which can overwrite an existing shortcut mapping; getGrantTypeByShortcut() resolves collisions with a stream().findFirst() over factories, which is not guaranteed deterministic, and then inserts the result. This can make token-id decoding for a given shortcut resolve to the wrong grant type after runtime registration, with no exception raised (the postInit check won’t re-run).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice and never validates rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId passes construction and encodeTokenId silently emits a token id ending in the literal string ':null'. The second check on line 71 was clearly meant to guard rawTokenId; as written, a caller that constructs an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets no error at construction and produces a jti whose unique-id suffix is the constant string 'null' -- colliding across every such token and defeating any per-token use of the id (revocation, event correlation). Latent today because the only in-diff caller passes KeycloakModelUtils.generateId(), but the guard the code visibly intends to provide does not exist.
matched_golden_ids: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same constructor bug: Objects.requireNonNull is applied to grantType twice and rawTokenId is never validated, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass. It even describes the intended fix (second check should guard rawTokenId) and the consequence of null rawTokenId.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The isAccessTokenId matcher checks the wrong character positions AND inverts the comparison: `items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` reads chars 4-5 (second char of tokenType + first char of grantType) instead of chars 5-6 (substring(4,6) where the grant shortcut lives), and it returns false when the shortcut MATCHES instead of when it mismatches. The grant-type assertion is inert in both directions: no real encoded prefix (st2+tt2+gt2, e.g. 'onrtac') can have chars at index 3-4 equal to any registered shortcut ('ac','cc','rt','ci','dg','ro','pg','te','pc'), so `matchesSafely` falls through to the UUID check and accepts ANY '<6chars>:<uuid>' token ID regardless of which grant type (or no grant type at all) was encoded. Every updated expectation (expectCodeToToken, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectAuthReqIdToToken) therefore passes even if TokenManager/initToken encodes the wrong grant, no grant, or a scrambled prefix — the suite gives false confidence that the new context encoding works end-to-end. Note also that fixing only the index while keeping the inverted compare would make every valid token FAIL, so the matcher as committed demonstrably never validated real encoder output.

adjudication.rationale: In AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId, the grant shortcut is encoded as the last 2 chars of the 6-char prefix (st(2)+tt(2)+gt(2)), i.e. indexes 4-5, but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5), which instead spans the 2nd char of tokenType plus the 1st char of grantType. Additionally, the logic is inverted: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects when it matches rather than when it mismatches. As written, the grant-type check does not correctly validate the encoded grant shortcut and will generally fall through to only checking that the suffix is a UUID, weakening the intended end-to-end test assertions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice — the fourth check at line 72 duplicates the grantType check (line 71) instead of checking rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is silently accepted. A caller passing null rawTokenId bypasses validation and later produces a token id like 'onrtna:null' from encodeTokenId (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java line ~120 concatenates getRawTokenId() unconditionally); no test in the diff covers this because the unit tests only pass literal non-null ids. The bug is self-evidencing: the error message even says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed' while the code checks grantType.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the 4th null-check mistakenly calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java` constructor). This allows `rawTokenId` to be null without throwing, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)` later concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()` unconditionally, producing an encoded id with the literal `null` if a null rawTokenId is passed. The mismatch is self-evident because the error message mentions `rawTokenId` while checking `grantType` again. The added tests only use non-null ids and wouldn’t catch this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext — the encode direction that TokenManager.initToken (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/TokenManager.java, initToken change at lines ~1048-1054) actually uses in production — is exercised by no test in this diff; only the decode direction is unit-tested. The branching logic that classifies tokens (TRANSIENT vs isOffline vs ONLINE, getShouldUseLightweightToken, null GRANT_TYPE attribute -> UNKNOWN) is the code that runs on every issued access token, and a regression there (e.g. misclassifying offline sessions, or reading the attribute under the wrong key) produces systematically wrong encoded token ids with no failing test. Evidence of absence: checked services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java (only calls getTokenContextFromTokenId and encodeTokenId on hand-built AccessTokenContext values) and testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java (whose matcher, per the bug above, verifies only 'prefix:uuid' shape).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds production usage of `TokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)` in `TokenManager.initToken()` (`encoder.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(clientSessionCtx, ...)` and then `encodeTokenId`). However, the new unit test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` only exercises the decode path (`getTokenContextFromTokenId`) and re-encoding of a prebuilt `AccessTokenContext` via `encodeTokenId`, and never calls `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`. Therefore the newly introduced branching logic in `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (TRANSIENT vs OFFLINE/ONLINE, `getShouldUseLightweightToken`, and null `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` -> `UNKNOWN`) is not covered by tests in this diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The test setup hand-populates the package-private maps `factory.grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` and never calls postInit, so the factory's real registration logic — the duplicate-shortcut validation in postInit (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java postInit, IllegalStateException check) and the lazy-refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut — has zero coverage. A future grant factory added with a shortcut colliding with an existing one (exactly the failure mode the postInit validation comment says it exists for) ships undetected, and the cluster-rolling-deploy lazy-refresh code paths (getShortcutByGrantType falling through to sessionFactory.getProviderFactory) — which contain non-trivial concurrency-prone map mutation — run in production with no test ever having executed them. adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the new test `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.before()` calls `factory.init(null)` and then directly assigns `factory.grantsByShortcuts` / `factory.grantsToShortcuts` (package-private fields in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory`) without ever invoking `postInit(KeycloakSessionFactory)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] testIncorrectGrantType catches broad RuntimeException with an empty 'ignored' handler and asserts nothing about the exception type or message, so any RuntimeException — including an NPE thrown by a bug in the parsing code rather than the intended IllegalArgumentException — passes the test. A regression that turns the deliberate IllegalArgumentException for a bad grant shortcut into an accidental NPE or IndexOutOfBoundsException (e.g. from substring on a malformed prefix) keeps this test green, and the '// ignored' handler swallows the evidence; the variable is even named 'iae' while catching RuntimeException, showing the intended narrower contract was loosened during writing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor validates grantType twice — `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed");` is repeated on the line that was meant to check rawTokenId — so a null rawTokenId passes validation unchallenged. A caller constructing an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId gets no validation failure; encodeTokenId then concatenates the null, minting a token id like 'onrtac:null' (string 'null' as the jti) instead of failing fast. No current caller in this diff passes null, so it is latent, but the guard this new public API promises does not exist for rawTokenId.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the last null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (see `AccessTokenContext.java`). This means `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast, and `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` will then concatenate `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, producing an encoded token id ending with `:null` rather than rejecting it. The duplicated validation is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Token-ID decoding is asymmetric across deployment transitions: legacy colonless IDs degrade gracefully to UNKNOWN context, but an encoded ID whose grant shortcut no longer maps (grant provider uninstalled/renamed between deployments) throws IllegalArgumentException from getTokenContextFromTokenId. Tokens issued while a (custom or later-removed) grant provider was registered persist their 2-char shortcut inside the id; after that provider is removed, any caller of getTokenContextFromTokenId — the method's stated purpose is to read context back out of long-lived tokens — gets an IllegalArgumentException instead of a UNKNOWN-context fallback, the exact treatment the same method grants to pre-upgrade UUID ids. The one migration-compat path built into this design (legacy IDs) is not applied to the second class of pre-existing data it will encounter: IDs minted by providers that no longer exist.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId(String)`: legacy IDs without `:` return an UNKNOWN context, but encoded IDs with an unmapped grant shortcut throw. Specifically, after parsing `gtShortcut`, the code does `String gt = factory.getGrantTypeByShortcut(gtShortcut); if (gt == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException(...) }` (no fallback). `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getGrantTypeByShortcut` only refreshes by scanning currently-registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` instances; if a previously-installed/now-removed grant (custom or renamed) minted tokens with a shortcut that no longer exists, `gt` remains null and decoding fails. This creates asymmetric/migration-breaking behavior for pre-existing token IDs compared to colonless (pre-upgrade) IDs, which the method explicitly handles gracefully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] initToken silently changes the persisted/emitted token identifier format from a 36-char UUID to a 43+ char 'prefix:uuid' form with no consumer-side compatibility step beyond the in-server decoder fallback. Every consumer that stores or joins on access-token ids — event-store TOKEN_ID details (the diff itself has to rewrite AssertEvents matchers for exactly this reason), external audit pipelines, or any tooling keyed on UUID format — receives a structurally different identifier after upgrade with no versioning or opt-out; records written before the upgrade (bare UUIDs) and after (prefixed) become a mixed-format column for such consumers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff verifiably changes `TokenManager.initToken()` from `token.id(KeycloakModelUtils.generateId())` (a bare UUID) to an encoded form via `TokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId(...)`, which returns a 6-char context prefix + `:` + raw UUID (e.g., `trltcc:1234` in the new unit test), i.e., ~43 chars. Tests in `AssertEvents` are updated to match this new structure for `Details.TOKEN_ID`, confirming externally visible event payloads change format. While the server-side decoder (`getTokenContextFromTokenId`) has a fallback for old IDs without `:`, the diff shows no compatibility/versioning/opt-out mechanism for external consumers that expect UUID-only token IDs, making this a real backward-compatibility/consumer-impact concern rather than a direct correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...) twice; the second call passes grantType with the message 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', so rawTokenId is never validated. A null rawTokenId passes the guard instead of failing fast, and encodeTokenId string-concats it into a literal token ID ending in ':null' (e.g. 'onrtac:null'); the only defense is the double-check that was supposed to reject it, so a caller passing a null raw ID gets a silently corrupt token identity rather than the NPE the guard promises.

adjudication.rationale: In `AccessTokenContext` constructor, the fourth null-check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` instead of checking `rawTokenId` (diff shows `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`). This means `rawTokenId` can be null without failing fast. Later `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId()` concatenates `':' + tokenContext.getRawTokenId()`, so a null raw ID would yield an encoded token id ending with `:null`, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GRANT_TYPE is only populated at the four explicit setAttribute sites (createTokenResponse, TokenManager.validateToken, StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient, PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType, ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType); any token-issuance path that builds its response outside these sites silently encodes grant context as UNKNOWN. Tokens issued on a path that does not route through createTokenResponse (e.g. token-exchange flows handled in AbstractTokenExchangeProvider outside exchangeClientToOIDCClient, or grant types that build AccessTokenResponseBuilder directly) get 'na' encoded in their jti with no log and no error — the encoder's purpose (distinguishing grant context from the token ID) silently degrades exactly on the paths someone forgot to touch, and nobody can detect it because UNKNOWN is a first-class accepted value that encodes and decodes successfully.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext()` reads `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, String.class)` and falls back to `UNKNOWN` (`"na"`) when absent, and the factory explicitly registers UNKNOWN so it encodes/decodes successfully. The only places in the diff that actually set the attribute are `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)`, `TokenManager.validateToken(...)`, `StandardTokenExchangeProvider.exchangeClientToOIDCClient(...)`, `PreAuthorizedCodeGrantType.process(...)`, and `ResourceOwnerPasswordCredentialsGrantType.process(...)`. Therefore, any access-token issuance path that calls `TokenManager.initToken()` without first setting `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` will silently encode `na` into the token id, degrading the new “grant context in jti” feature without any error. The finding’s examples (other token-exchange paths / other builders) are plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The lazy refresh in getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut puts into the maps with no duplicate-shortcut check, so a runtime-discovered grant factory whose shortcut collides with an existing grant's shortcut silently overwrites the existing mapping that postInit's size-comparison validation was written to prevent. If a colliding grant factory ever reaches this lazy path, tokens of the displaced grant still encode with the old shortcut but decode (getGrantTypeByShortcut) to the new grant's ID — grant type is silently misattributed on decode with no error, the exact corruption the postInit IllegalStateException exists to catch; the check-then-put race between two concurrent first-encounters is benign, but the overwrite is not. Also note this lazy path is effectively unreachable under the normal Keycloak lifecycle (postInit already enumerates all OAuth2GrantTypeFactories via getProviderFactoriesStream), making it dead defensive code carrying this footgun.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory, postInit() builds grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts and validates uniqueness via a size comparison, but the later “lazy refresh” code paths can overwrite existing mappings without any duplicate-shortcut validation. Specifically, getShortcutByGrantType() does grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) and grantsToShortcuts.put(grantType, shortcut), and getGrantTypeByShortcut() similarly does grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, newGrantType) if it finds a factory with that shortcut. If a newly discovered OAuth2GrantTypeFactory (or a factory not present during postInit) reuses an existing shortcut, the old mapping can be silently displaced, causing decode (shortcut→grant) to return a different grant than intended with no error—exactly what postInit’s uniqueness check aims to prevent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getTokenContextFromTokenId has an inconsistent failure shape: an ID with no colon degrades gracefully to UNKNOWN context (the legacy-token path), but any ID containing a colon whose prefix is not exactly 6 chars — or with unknown 2-char shortcuts — throws an unchecked IllegalArgumentException, and no caller in this diff catches it. The method's entire purpose is decoding token IDs it did not mint (legacy tokens, and eventually client-presented jtis in validation/introspection flows); whoever wires the first production caller and feeds it a token whose jti is not exactly '6chars:uuid' — a foreign-issuer token like 'abc:def', or a truncated value — gets a raw RuntimeException propagated up the request path as a 500 where a 4xx/handled-rejection belongs, while legacy UUIDs silently work, so the failure only appears for a subset of malformed inputs and is easy to ship untested.

adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromTokenId, the diff clearly shows two different behaviors: if no ':' is present it returns an AccessTokenContext with UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN and raw id, but if ':' is present and the prefix is not length 6 or any 2-char shortcut is unrecognized, it throws IllegalArgumentException. That inconsistency on malformed-but-colon-containing inputs is real and diff-grounded. However, within this diff there is no production call site added that invokes getTokenContextFromTokenId on untrusted/request-provided JTIs (TokenManager only encodes token IDs), so the claim about uncaught exceptions causing 500s is speculative from the diff alone; the actionable issue is API/edge-case robustness rather than a currently verifiable broken behavior.
